fit: two ginger extract capsule strengths and composite motor complications
assessment: Official other outcomes list change in MDS-UPDRS Parts I–IV at 12 weeks. The record gives no separate dyskinesia item outcome, ground ginger, inactive comparator or results.

fit: oral corn oil with injected toxin and time to combined motor signs
assessment: Combined phenotype appeared in 14.00 versus 20.21 days (p<.0001) in the two toxin groups. Oil-only animals did not exhibit the composite during observation. Animal replacement, oil grade, composite timing and species limit transfer to clinical bradykinesia severity.

fit: oral hydroalcoholic leaf extract and rodent maze exploration
assessment: Elevated-plus-maze open-arm entries increased at two amounts and open-arm time at the highest. The preparation is a concentrated extract and the endpoint a rodent proxy.

fit: injected thyme essential oil and rodent behavior after BPA exposure
assessment: The open-field comparison favors more exploratory visits with the oil. The direction assigned to time in light or darkness raises interpretation uncertainty. The species, concentrated oil, route and model differ.

fit: aqueous wild-thyme extract and gastrointestinal anxiety quality-of-life domain
assessment: The FDDQL anxiety difference was +3.21 (95% CI −4.17 to 10.60, p=.410). The linked official record differs on design, sample, masking and primary outcome. Different species, extract and clinical setting.

fit: oral solvent-extracted flaxseed oil and rodent wet stools
assessment: Wet feces increased at the two lower oil amounts but approached vehicle at the higher amount. The Methods document petroleum-ether extraction. No human symptom score or Parkinson cohort.
